iam-1.finding: The partner router requires authentication, but the routes in server.js have no authentication middleware.
iam-1.fix: Mount authentication middleware on the application and list public routes explicitly.

iam-1.1.finding: The administrative export has no authentication, so it has no second factor either.
iam-1.1.fix: Require an administrator session with a second factor before the export runs.

iam-2.finding: The login compares the submitted password in a database query, so it is stored unhashed.
iam-2.fix: Store a salted hash with an approved function and verify it in application code.

iam-3.finding: signJwt is not part of the repository, so the token lifetime cannot be read from the source.

iam-4.finding: The partner router authenticates each call and selects orders by the authenticated partner.

iam-4.1.finding: The key lookup is implemented outside the repository, so key storage and rotation cannot be read from the source.

iam-5.finding: Any caller can read any user record by changing the identifier in the URL.
iam-5.fix: Compare the requested user with the authenticated identity before the query.

iam-6.finding: The tenant comes from a request header that the client controls.
iam-6.fix: Read the tenant from the authenticated identity.

iam-7.finding: The administrative export has no role check.
iam-7.fix: Check the administrator role on the server for each call.

inp-1.finding: Both queries are built by joining strings with request data.

inp-2.finding: A request field reaches a shell command.
inp-2.fix: Start tar without a shell and check the path against an allow-list.

inp-3.finding: The server fetches any URL from the request body.
inp-3.fix: Check the destination against an allow-list and refuse internal addresses.

inp-4.finding: The redirect target comes from the query string without a check.
inp-4.fix: Accept only relative paths or allow-listed hosts.

inp-5.finding: Request bodies are parsed but never validated against a schema.
inp-5.fix: Validate each request body against a schema at the route.

sec-1.finding: A signing secret and a database password are stored in the repository.
sec-1.fix: Replace both values and load them from the secrets manager at runtime.

sec-2.finding: The service listens on plain HTTP, but TLS may end at a proxy that the repository does not show.

sec-3.finding: The catalog leaves the rotation interval open, and the repository shows no rotation process.

log-1.finding: The login handler records no authentication outcome.
log-1.fix: Log each outcome with time, identity and source, without credentials.

log-2.finding: The export route returns a raw system error message to the client.
log-2.fix: Return a generic message and keep the details in the server log.

log-3.finding: A debug route returns the full process environment.
log-3.fix: Remove the route from production builds.

sup-1.finding: The workflow pins actions to a movable tag.
sup-1.fix: Pin each action to a full commit hash.

sup-2.finding: CI and the image build run npm install without a committed lock file.
sup-2.fix: Commit a lock file and use npm ci.

sup-3.finding: lodash 4.17.10 has publicly known critical vulnerabilities.
sup-3.fix: Upgrade lodash to a fixed release.

sup-4.finding: The image sets no USER, so the service starts as root.
sup-4.fix: Add a non-root USER before the start command.

sup-4.1.finding: The base image is pinned to a movable tag.
sup-4.1.fix: Pin the base image to a digest.

ai-1.finding: User input is joined directly into the instruction text of the prompt.
ai-1.fix: Pass user input as a separate message and treat it as data.

ai-2.finding: Model output is sent to the client without encoding or validation.
ai-2.fix: Encode or validate the output before it leaves the service.

ai-3.finding: The approved provider list is not in the repository.

pay-1.finding: The service handles no card payments.
